extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (and NIH peer reviewers)/NIAID program staff
extracted.subtask_description: A peer review summary statement for an NIH G11 (Global Infectious Disease Research Administration Development Award) application, showing the standard review criteria, strengths/weaknesses identified by reviewers, and administrative determinations. Useful as an exemplar of NIH review expectations for capacity-building awards to foreign institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field and the potential for the project to have broad impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list explicit strengths and weaknesses. Strength examples from this application: responds to capacity building needs for research administration; leverages prior CaBERA-I work; capacity building for both administrators and faculty. Weakness examples: none noted in one critique; elsewhere concerns include lack of comprehensive assessment program to evaluate impact, and need for clearer evidence of demand from mentee institutions. Use these points to justify the Significance score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the PI and key personnel: their qualifications, experience, and ability to carry out the proposed work and lead the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: PI has relevant experience, authority and passion; prior successful completion of CaBERA; strong collaborating staff at Yale and commitment from key staff. Weakness examples: one critique notes lack of specifics about research administration personnel roles and responsibilities at NMIMR. Reviewers consider prior performance and demonstrated ability to accomplish objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application proposes novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies, or an innovative application of existing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: expansion to other institutions in the region perceived as innovative; mentoring across institutions seen as meritorious. Weakness examples: proposed activities are incremental/standard and do not utilize novel concepts or new strategies; lacks new ideas for improving institutional grants management. Use innovation assessment to judge novelty versus incremental build-on of prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the strategy, methodology, timeline, and whether the plan is well-reasoned, feasible, and includes appropriate milestones, benchmarks, alternatives, and mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: needs assessment-driven training plan; well-reasoned timeline; builds on prior success; plans for recruitment, training, refresher courses, and sustainability efforts. Weakness examples: lacks detail on benchmarks for success, alternative strategies, mitigation plans, mentoring junior staff, specifics on changing institutional grants management practices, and selection criteria for mentee institutions; inconsistencies in effort and funds requested. Reviewers expect clear metrics, contingency plans, and operational details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the institutional support, facilities, resources, and collaborative environment that will contribute to project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: institutional support provided; committed key staff; Yale collaboration and adequate IT/infrastructure; leadership support. Weakness examples: insufficient description of administrative environment, coordination/communication plans with mentee institutions, and lack of letters of collaboration from mentee institutions. Reviewers look for concrete institutional commitments and infrastructure detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers' overall assessment of the application’s likely impact if fully realized, resulting in a numerical impact/priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring procedure described: the impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted by individual assigned reviewers prior to the meeting and are not discussed or calculated into the overall impact score at the meeting. Applications may also receive a percentile. Use the overall impact to synthesize strengths/weaknesses across criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of applicability and adequacy of protections for human subjects. (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard review checklist item. If applicable, reviewers evaluate risks, protections, benefits, and monitoring. In this summary, human subjects protections were marked 'Not applicable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application addresses inclusion of women in research (applicability determined per study). (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard NIH inclusion consideration; when applicable reviewers assess adequacy of plans to include women. Marked not applicable for this application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the application addresses inclusion of minority groups in research (applicability determined per study). (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard NIH inclusion consideration; when applicable reviewers assess plans and justification. Marked not applicable for this application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Individuals Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of inclusion across age ranges where relevant. (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard NIH inclusion consideration; when applicable reviewers assess inclusion across lifespan. Marked not applicable here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of applicability and justification for use of vertebrate animals. (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard checklist item for animal research. In this application, marked 'No live vertebrate animals involved for competing appl.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data / Model Organism / Genomic Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of data sharing, model organism sharing, and genomic data sharing plans. (Here: Data sharing plan, model organism sharing plan, genomic data sharing plan all marked NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers evaluate adequacy and feasibility of sharing plans. If not applicable, state as such. This summary marks these plans N/A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to authenticate key biological/chemical resources. (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers examine documentation/plan for resource authentication. Marked N/A in this summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Review determination about whether the foreign institution's participation is justified and acceptable (here: FOREIGN INSTITUTION: JUSTIFIED — Ghana).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications from foreign institutions, reviewers/commenters assess justification for foreign location and any special considerations. This entry indicates the committee judged the foreign institution justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether there is overlap between proposed budgetary items and other funding/support. (Here: NOT APPLICABLE.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers check for duplicative or overlapping funding. Marked N/A in this summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Budget Recommendations / Administrative Budget Note
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee recommendation regarding the budget and a note that the budget shown is the requested budget and may be adjusted by grants management if an award is planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application: 'The budget is recommended as requested in all years.' Administrative note: costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff based on committee recommendations; budget shown not adjusted to reflect reviewer recommendations. Use this section to communicate budgetary recommendation separate from scientific review.
